The opening quiz is on this reading.

## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Linear regression, non-linear models, and count models — described, not derived: what each estimates and how to read a coefficient in the units of the problem. Then where uncertainty comes from: residuals and errors, sampling variation, what a standard error states, where p-values come from and what they are not. Finally the distinction that decides half the projects in this room — explaining versus predicting, and why a model that predicts well may tell you nothing about what to do

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team stand-up: what you did,
what is blocked, and who does what next — in writing, submitted with
the session output.

Simulation lab: draw from a world you control. Watch the p-value distribution under the null, then change the sample size and the variation and watch it move. Then fit the same world in-sample and out-of-sample, and watch a model that looks excellent fail on data it has not seen. Nothing to install, no code to write

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.
